title: The invitation
logline: Cream cardstock on the drafting table. Wood frames it — at the frame shop he no longer works at, after hours, with Gully's key.

panels.composition: The garage. The invitation on the drafting table: cream, letterpress, a pressed fern. WOOD looking at it. BARNABY.
props: letterpress invitation with a pressed fern

image.prompt: a letterpress wedding invitation on cream cardstock with a pressed fern lying on a garage drafting table, a thin man looking at it, an old dog, razor-sharp ink

panels.composition: The frame shop, night, closed. GULLY unlocking the side door with a key. Wood behind him with the invitation and the dog.

balloons.text: Why do you have a key.
Since you got let go. Someone had to keep an eye.

image.prompt: a stocky man unlocking the side door of a dark closed shop at night with a key, a thin man behind him carrying an old dog and a card

panels.composition: Wood at the mat cutter, in the dark shop, one lamp. Cutting a mat for the invitation. Cream and green. A forty-five. His hands remember.

image.prompt: close-up of hands cutting a double mat in cream and green at a mat cutter in a dark shop under one lamp, clean line, no words

panels.composition: The invitation framed, cedar, on the garage wall beside 'Lanes.' Wood looking at it. Gully in the door. The dog asleep. Nobody says the thing.

image.prompt: a wedding invitation framed in plain cedar hanging on a garage wall beside a framed watercolor, a thin man looking at it, a stocky man in the doorway, an old dog asleep, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: He frames the invitation. Gully has a key because he fixes the furnace. 'Someone had to keep an eye.'
